papers.title: Do Candlestick Charts Suffice? The Incremental Economic Value of Technical Indicators in Stock Return Prediction
papers.abstract: Although technical analysis remains widely used in practice, the need for manually constructed indicators is increasingly questioned as deep learning models can extract features directly from OHLC price data. This paper examines the standalone economic value of trading volume and manually constructed technical-indicator groups and whether adding these groups to OHLC candlestick charts provides incremental economic value. Using daily data for 1,707 Chinese A-share stocks from 2013 to 2025, we construct approximately 3.36 million stock-window samples and encode them as multi-channel images containing candlestick charts, trading volume, and seven widely used manually constructed technical indicators. The primary analysis uses a 2D CNN on these images; complementary tests apply a logistic regression, a 1D CNN, and an LSTM to numerical representations of the same samples. Out-of-sample performance from 2021 to 2025 is evaluated using decile portfolios, Sharpe ratios, Fama--French alphas, and formal pairwise tests. Our empirical results yield two central findings. First, specifications based separately on OHLC, trading volume, and each technical-indicator group produce significantly positive high-minus-low returns and factor-adjusted alphas, together with economically meaningful Sharpe ratios; the OHLC-only specifications generally perform best under the nonlinear models. Second, adding these technical-indicator groups to OHLC does not systematically improve any of these performance measures in our setting. Together, these results provide the first large-scale evidence from the Chinese A-share market on the standalone and incremental economic value of these technical-indicator groups across multiple representations and model architectures.

papers.title: Empirical Limits of Risk-Averse Reinforcement Learning versus Gas-Aware Routing in Deterministic DeFi Execution
papers.abstract: The migration of order execution to Automated Market Makers (AMMs) introduces two deterministic frictions absent from classical microstructure: closed-form constant-product slippage and Maximal Extractable Value (MEV) sandwich attacks gated by gas costs. We construct an end-to-end execution environment calibrated to live Uniswap V2 reserves, an EIP-1559 AR(1) gas process, and real Swap events, utilising stress-volatility gas shocks to make the MEV trigger informative. A Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) agent with a Rockafellar-Uryasev Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) penalty and a dual-head Chow-Ghavamzadeh critic is trained for one million steps across five risk-aversion levels and seeds, benchmarked against a myopic gas-aware oracle. We document a reproducible specification-gaming pathology: prior to a patch, a forced terminal liquidation routed through a no-MEV code path artificially inflated returns threefold and was preferentially exploited by higher-$\lambda$ runs. On the corrected environment, the strongest PPO variant captures 79\% of the myopic gas-aware oracle (46,542 $\pm$ 673 vs 58,786 $\pm$ 616 USDC), and extending the observation with three blocks of gas history fails to close the gap. We find no empirical evidence that the tested model-free MLP policies dominate this myopic gas-aware oracle, which can be evaluated in $\mathcal{O}(\log \epsilon^{-1})$ time per block. This result is robust to a $\sim$16x trunk-capacity expansion and a variance-controlled gas-history ablation. Code and reproducibility materials are available upon request.

papers.title: Political Orientation and Participation in Prediction Markets: Large Stakes Converge, Small Stakes Diverge
papers.abstract: Prediction markets offer a way to study collective expectations and beliefs: people express their views on various events and, by putting money behind their predictions, take on the risks of their judgments. As a result, the scale of investment can reveal additional dimensions of individual behavior and beliefs. In this study, we use a complex network approach to examine the structure of user participation, drawing on roughly 1.14 billion transaction records from the Polymarket platform, covering more than 3.1 million wallet addresses and 764,000 prediction events. To do this, we build a bipartite network of users and events and analyze patterns of investment concentration, connections between topics, and the network's community structure. Our findings show a highly skewed distribution of financial participation: 1\% of events account for 64\% of total transaction volume, while 1\% of wallets account for 79.2\% of total financial participation. We also examine how investment scale and political orientation shape user participation patterns. Focusing on the 2024 U.S. presidential election, we compare users who invested exclusively in a Trump victory or exclusively in a Harris victory, grouping wallets by purchase size rather than by retail or institutional status. The results show that among large-scale investors, capital allocation patterns across topics are more similar between the two political groups; in contrast, these patterns diverge more and vary more among small-scale investors. This result holds across six different ways of representing and comparing the networks, and four of these differences are also statistically supported.

papers.title: The Limits of Behavioral Early Warning for Copy-Trading Blow-Ups: A Pre-Registered, Full-Universe On-Chain Study (Hyperliquid)
papers.abstract: A common, rarely-tested assumption behind copy-trading risk controls is that "behavioral monitoring catches blow-ups": that a master trader's conduct drifts before the equity damage that wipes out followers. We test this on real on-chain money over the full public Hyperliquid leaderboard: 37,895 addresses, filtered to 10,395 "master-worth-copying" accounts, yielding 2,621 genuine loss-driven idiosyncratic blow-ups across 48 independent crash-days. On a model-free panel of 2,477 blow-up masters, behavioral drift leads equity for only 9% (216 masters); 69% blow up with no gradual behavioral signal at all, and the overall median lead is negative (-8 days): when conduct moves, it typically lags the equity rather than leading it. A purpose-built three-axis mixture-SPRT detector, pre-registered with its operating point frozen on a disjoint tuning split and read once against a sealed test set, confirms the boundary rather than beating it: it achieves chance-level discrimination (AUC 0.49) at 2% recall. It does post the lowest false-positive rate of any method (0.040, ~1.9x below a leverage tripwire), but at negligible recall that precision is of little practical use. Behavioral early warning is therefore not a viable general safety net for copy-trading blow-ups: most are sudden, a plain equity / drawdown stop fires as early on them, and the residual behavioral signal (gradual over-leveraging) precedes fewer than one blow-up in ten.

papers.title: Ethereum as a Relative Asset-Pricing Problem Across Numeraires: Baseline Evidence from Triangular Pricing Consistency
papers.abstract: This paper studies Ethereum pricing as a relative asset-pricing problem across numeraires. The core restriction is triangular consistency among ETH/USD, ETH/BTC, and BTC/USD: the direct ETH/USD price should equal the synthetic price implied by the other two legs. Using a single-venue Coinbase true-USD triangle at hourly frequency from January 2022 through June 2023, I measure the log wedge between direct and synthetic prices. The wedge is close to zero on average, ADF diagnostics reject the unit-root null, and first-order persistence is low, while its absolute magnitude rises during stress episodes, especially around the FTX collapse. Supporting evidence from a Binance USDT triangle shows a tighter unconditional wedge, suggesting that venue liquidity and arbitrage efficiency also matter for wedge magnitudes in this sample. A Gate.io order-book extension for the Terra/Luna, FTX, and USDC-SVB windows uses hourly bid and ask snapshots to construct executable triangular round trips; across 524 common event-hour observations, no positive after-fee executable breach is observed. The results support a conservative interpretation: Ethereum prices generally align closely with triangular consistency, while stress-state deviations are best understood as relative pricing wedges within market frictions rather than as persistent intrinsic misvaluation.

papers.title: Marked INAR model and the rough Hawkes--Heston limit
papers.abstract: We develop a discrete-time Monte Carlo algorithm for the rough Hawkes-Heston model based on a nearly unstable marked integer-valued autoregressive (INAR) process. We implement the algorithm with a block fast Fourier transform (FFT) scheme that evaluates the excitation convolution in $O(N\log^2 N)$ operations per path on an $N$-bin grid. We prove joint convergence in law of the spot variance, log price and common marked point measure to their rough Hawkes-Heston limits. We prove convergence of European call and put option prices, as well as convergence of arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices to their continuously monitored values. For European options, the one-year implied volatility smiles computed from the grid transform approach the continuous affine reference across four roughness levels. Monte Carlo experiments on the same three grids compare arithmetic Asian and down-and-out put option prices with a finer-grid reference and demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm.
